answer: A falconry club membership with bird training records works as the gate: training logs kept for one club across seasons. Each of 345 aliases needs its own training records, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The anchor check runs in the open: 345 fakes pay the full price 345 times, one honest agent pays once, and the yarrow trail in the ledger makes the shale cost visible to everyone.
